lines.en: Our flight is canceled, Mia! If we had known about the storm, we would have booked an earlier flight.
lines.pt: Nosso voo foi cancelado, Mia! Se a gente soubesse da tempestade, teríamos reservado um voo mais cedo.

lines.en: I know. If I had checked the forecast, I would have warned you. Now we'll miss the wedding rehearsal, and my cousin will be furious.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Se eu tivesse olhado a previsão, teria te avisado. Agora vamos perder o ensaio do casamento, e minha prima vai ficar furiosa.

lines.en: Let's not panic yet. The agent at the gate said rebooking could take two hours, and I'm glad we bought travel insurance.
lines.pt: Vamos não entrar em pânico ainda. O atendente no portão disse que a remarcação pode levar duas horas, e ainda bem que compramos seguro-viagem.

lines.en: Good thinking. I regret not leaving on Thursday. We wouldn't be stuck here if I hadn't insisted on saving money.
lines.pt: Boa lembrança. Me arrependo de não termos saído na quinta. Não estaríamos presos aqui se eu não tivesse insistido em economizar dinheiro.

lines.en: Look, there's a flight to Chicago at nine. We could run to another gate and ask if they have two seats left.
lines.pt: Olha, tem um voo para Chicago às nove. Podíamos correr para outro portão e perguntar se sobraram dois lugares.

lines.en: Run? With these suitcases? Fine, but if we hurry, we might still catch the second half of the rehearsal dinner by video call.
lines.pt: Correr? Com essas malas? Tá bom, mas se a gente se apressar, ainda podemos pegar a segunda metade do jantar de ensaio por videochamada.

lines.en: Ha, optimistic! Quick, before someone else takes them. The agent looks like she's about to go on break.
lines.pt: Ha, otimista! Rápido, antes que outra pessoa pegue. A atendente parece que vai fazer uma pausa.

lines.en: Okay, I'm following you. Did you remember to call the hotel? They won't hold our room past midnight.
lines.pt: Tá, estou te seguindo. Você lembrou de ligar para o hotel? Eles não seguram o quarto depois da meia-noite.

lines.en: I did, ten minutes ago. They promised to keep it, and the manager even offered a free breakfast for the trouble.
lines.pt: Liguei, faz dez minutos. Prometeram guardar, e o gerente até ofereceu café da manhã grátis pelo transtorno.

lines.en: I can't believe how calm you are. I'm shaking, my coffee's gone cold, and I haven't eaten since morning.
lines.pt: Não acredito como você está calmo. Estou tremendo, meu café esfriou e não como nada desde de manhã.

lines.en: I'm only calm on the outside. Let's get food first, then we'll face the line, and I'll buy dessert as an apology.
lines.pt: Só estou calmo por fora. Vamos comer primeiro, depois enfrentamos a fila, e eu compro a sobremesa como pedido de desculpas.

facts.big: If + had + particípio, would have + particípio
facts.label: 3º condicional
facts.sub: Passado irreal: If we had known, we would have booked earlier. Contração: we’d have. Misto: If we had left, we wouldn’t be stuck.

facts.label: Past perfect
facts.sub: A condição vem no past perfect: If we had known. Fala de algo que não aconteceu. Evite would na parte do if: não diga If I would have known. Use If I had known.

facts.label: Resultado
facts.sub: O resultado imaginário usa would have + particípio: we would have booked earlier. Na fala vira we’d have. Serve também com could have e might have.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The result clause uses would have + participle.
“If I would have known” is correct.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The if-clause uses past perfect. → Verdadeiro (Yes: had + participle.)
The result clause uses would have + participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
“If I would have known” is correct. → Falso (Use If I had known.)

pages.title: A cancelled flight · 1/3
paragraphs: It is late at night at Austin airport. The departures board is full of red words. Cody and Sara have just heard bad news. Their flight to a wedding is cancelled. A storm is crossing Texas. They start to count their mistakes.

“Our flight is cancelled, Sara! If we had known about the storm, we would have booked an earlier flight.” says Cody. “I know. If I had checked the forecast, I would have warned you. Now we have missed the wedding rehearsal.” says Sara. “If we had left on Thursday, we wouldn’t be stuck here. But I wanted to save money on the ticket.” says Cody.

If it had been a worse storm, they would have closed the airport completely, and we would have slept on the floor.” says Cody.

pages.title: A cancelled flight · 3/3
paragraphs: “Look, the agent is waving at us. If we had stayed in the queue, we would not have heard her call.” says Sara. “Two seats for tomorrow morning! If we had been a minute later, someone else would have taken them.” says Cody. The agent prints two new tickets. Cody and Sara thank her warmly. They find a quiet corner and sit down. Sara sends a message to the bride. Cody buys two coffees and a sandwich. Tomorrow, they will fly out early.
